definition: The number of minutes, within any 10-minute period, a process can run at a given current without the machine overheating and shutting down. Formula: minutes_welding = dutyCyclePercent / 100 * 10; minutes_resting = 10 - minutes_welding.
note: Each process has three rated points per input voltage (25/30/40% depending on process, 60%, 100%). All values below are cross-verified between the nameplate table (page 14) and the per-process narrative sections (pages 19, 29); the two sources agree on every point.

FluxCored.note: The manual's published duty-cycle nameplate table and Specifications table (page 7) give MIG/Stick/TIG figures only; Flux-Cored is not separately rated in the source material and shares the machine's MIG-mode power path. Do not present a Flux-Cored-specific duty cycle number as documented fact — say the manual does not publish one separately and point to the MIG figures as the closest documented reference.

thermalProtection.behavior: The welder has an internal thermal protection system. On overheat it shuts down automatically and shows a warning screen on the LCD. It resumes automatically after cooling (leave the Power Switch ON so the internal fan can cool it). After a shutdown, rest the gun/torch/electrode holder on a non-conductive, heat-proof surface away from the ground clamp, then use shorter welding periods and longer rests.
